facts.statement: Tototlmimus was an extinct ornithomimid theropod dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) in Sonora, Mexico.
facts.quote: Tototlmimus is an extinct genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) Packard Formation of Sonora, Mexico.

facts.statement: The species Tototlmimus packardensis was formally described in October 2015 by Claudia Inés Serrano-Brañas and colleagues.
facts.quote: The only known species, the type species Tototlmimus packardensis, was formally described in October 2015 by Claudia Inés Serrano-Brañas, Esperanza Torres-Rodríguez, Paola Carolina Reyes-Luna, Ixchel González-Ramírez and Carlos González-León

facts.statement: The genus name Tototlmimus is derived from the Nahuatl word for 'bird' and the Latin word for 'mimic'.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the Nahuatl word tototl, bird, and the Latin mimus, mimic (from Greek μῖμος).

facts.statement: The specific name packardensis refers to the fossil's origin in the Packard Formation.
facts.quote: The specific name refers to its origin from the Packard Formation.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ERNO 8553 was found in the Cabullona Group of Sonora, Mexico, and dates to approximately 72 million years ago.
facts.quote: The fossil specimen, holotype ERNO 8553, was found in the northeastern Mexican state of Sonora, in the Cabullona Group, in a bed of the Packard Shale which may date from the late Campanian, 72 million years ago.

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton that lacks a skull.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton without skull.

facts.statement: Tototlmimus is classified as a medium-sized ornithomimid dinosaur.
facts.quote: Tototlmimus is a medium-sized ornithomimid.

facts.statement: The third metatarsal of Tototlmimus has a weakly developed ginglymoid inferior articular surface.
facts.quote: The third metatarsal has an only weakly developed ginglymoid inferior articular surface.

facts.statement: The foot claws of Tototlmimus are narrow, asymmetric, and have shallow grooves on both sides.
facts.quote: The unguals, the bones of the foot claws, are narrow and asymmetric with shallow grooves on both sides.

facts.statement: Tototlmimus possesses a typical ornithomimosaur foot structure known as an arctometatarsus, where the third metatarsal narrows at the top.
facts.quote: Tototlmimus shows a foot with a typical build for ornithomimosaurs. The midfoot is an arctometatarsus, with a third metatarsal that becomes narrower at the top.

facts.statement: Tototlmimus is classified within the family Ornithomimidae in a derived position.
facts.quote: Tototlmimus was placed in the Ornithomimidae, in a derived position.

facts.statement: Tototlmimus is the first named ornithomimid from Mexico and represents one of the southernmost known species in North America.
facts.quote: It is the first ornithomimid named from Mexico and one of the southernmost known in North America.

facts.statement: Cladistic analysis suggests that Tototlmimus is the sister genus to Ornithomimus.
facts.quote: According to a cladistic analysis in the scientific description, it was the sister genus of Ornithomimus.

facts.statement: Tototlmimus packardensis was the only known species of this extinct ornithomimid theropod, living in North America during the Late Cretaceous (Campanian) 72 million years ago.
facts.quote: Tototlmimus packardensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Tototlmimus de dinosaurio terópodo ornitomímido que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace 72 millones de años durante el Campaniano, en lo que es hoy Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The third metatarsal of Tototlmimus has a barely developed ginglymoid inferior articular surface.
facts.quote: El tercer metatarsiano tiene una superficie articular inferior gingliomoidea apenas desarrollada.

facts.statement: The claw bone (ungual) of Tototlmimus is narrow and asymmetric with shallow grooves on both sides.
facts.quote: La falange ungueal, el hueso de la garra, es estrecha y asimétrica con surcos poco profundos a ambos lados.

facts.statement: The foot claw of Tototlmimus lacks a deep longitudinal groove for the flexor muscle tendon but has a deep groove on its lower inner side near the articulation surface.
facts.quote: La garra del pie no tiene un surco profundo longitudinal para el tendón del músculo flexor, pero tiene en cambio un surco profundo en su zona inferior interior, cerca de la superficie de la articulación.

facts.statement: The type species Tototlmimus packardensis was named and described in 2016 by Claudia Inés Serrano Brañas and colleagues.
facts.quote: La especie tipo Tototlmimus packardensis fue nombrada y descrita en 2016 por Claudia Inés Serrano Brañas, Esperanza Torres-Rodríguez, Paola Carolina Reyes-Luna, Ixchel González-González Ramírez y Carlos León.

facts.statement: The genus name is derived from the Nahuatl word tototl ('bird') and the ancient Greek word mimus ('imitator').
facts.quote: El nombre del género se deriva del término náhuatl tototl, "ave" y el griego antiguo mimus, "imitador".

facts.statement: The holotype fossil ERNO 8553 was found in northeastern Sonora, Mexico, in the Cabullona Group, dating to the late Campanian approximately 72 million years ago.
facts.quote: El espécimen fósil, el holotipo ERNO 8553, se encontró en el noreste del estado mexicano de Sonora, en el Grupo Cabullona, en una capa antigua de la Formación Packard que parece datar de finales del Campaniano, hace 72 millones de años.

facts.statement: The fossil specimen consists of a partial skeleton without a skull.
facts.quote: Se compone de un esqueleto parcial sin cráneo.

facts.statement: The fossil elements, none of which are complete, were found in an area of half a cubic meter.
facts.quote: Los elementos fósiles, ninguno de los cuales están completos, se encontraron en un área de medio metro cúbico.

facts.statement: Tototlmimus is placed in the family Ornithomimidae in a derived position.
facts.quote: Tototlmimus se sitúa en la familia Ornithomimidae, en una posición derivada.

facts.statement: Tototlmimus is the first designated ornithomimid from Mexico and one of the most southern known in North America.
facts.quote: Es el primer ornitomímido designado de México y uno de los más australes conocidos en América del Norte.

facts.statement: According to a cladistic analysis in its scientific description, Tototlmimus was the sister genus of Ornithomimus.
facts.quote: De acuerdo con un análisis cladístico realizado en su descripción científica, era el género hermano de Ornithomimus.

facts.statement: The time range for Tototlmimus is the Campanian stage, from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: because the online publication was not registered in ZooBank, the name was only validly published when the paper was printed in March 2016.
